summary: Remote-controlled shell PTY and self-update in @yeaft/webchat-agent
details: The package runs as a long-lived agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (SERVER_URL / AGENT_SECRET) and routes server-sent frames into local host operations. `handleTerminalCreate` spawns an interactive PTY via `pty.spawn(process.env.SHELL || 'bash')`, and `handleTerminalInput` writes WS-supplied `msg.data` directly into `term.pty.write`, giving the remote endpoint full interactive shell control of the host running the agent. A separate `upgrade_agent` WS handler triggers `npm install <pkg>@latest` (writing and spawning `upgrade.sh` on Unix or an equivalent runner on Windows) and restarts the service under systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the remote server force unattended package updates. `service/linux.js` also mutates PATH (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`) as part of service installation. The default `serverUrl` is loopback, but the SERVER_URL/config knob permits pointing the agent at any remote endpoint, and the terminal-input and upgrade handlers do not restrict who is on the other side of that socket beyond a shared secret.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
